purpose: Compare structural balance with current lived pain, fund the strongest remediable needs, and require recurring reassessment instead of permanently fixing every lane to a peer spending share.
core_rule: Peer position is context. Allocation follows evidenced pain, the expected outcome gain from a specific intervention, urgency, equity, and the capacity to deliver without breaching a floor.

cycle.name: measure
cycle.action: Refresh the common-year baseline, outcomes, access, affordability, reliability, distribution, obligations, and peer context for every lane.

cycle.name: protect
cycle.action: Fund legal commitments and minimum safety, access, readiness, adequacy, rights, and solvency floors before discretionary ranking.

cycle.name: diagnose
cycle.action: Identify acute pain, structural underperformance, inefficient excess, and cost shifting; do not infer need or waste from spending level alone.

cycle.name: rank_interventions
cycle.action: Compare specific interventions by pain severity, affected population, urgency, expected marginal outcome, evidence strength, equity, delivery capacity, and total public/private cost.

cycle.name: allocate
cycle.action: Assign temporary repair funds or recurring structural funds; keep an explicit reserve and avoid automatic lane entitlements.

cycle.name: deliver_and_monitor
cycle.action: Track outputs, outcomes, access, burden, implementation, displacement, and unintended cost shifts against dated milestones.

cycle.name: sunset_or_continue
cycle.action: Expire temporary funding unless the pain persists and the intervention works; continue structural funding only when the continuing obligation or durable value is demonstrated.

cycle.name: rebalance
cycle.action: Return realized savings, failed interventions, and released temporary funds to the next all-lane review, then repeat the cycle.

evaluation_dimensions.question: Is a legal, safety, access, readiness, adequacy, rights, resilience, or solvency floor breached or likely to be breached?
How severe is the measured harm relative to an explicit threshold?
How many people are affected, for how long, and which groups or places bear the burden?
What becomes more costly, dangerous, or irreversible if action waits?
What additional outcome is expected from the next dollar rather than from the program average?
How strong and transferable is the causal evidence for the specific intervention?
Can the responsible institutions absorb and deliver the funding on schedule?
Does the change reduce federal cost by shifting cost or risk to states, households, employers, or later years?
Is the lane outside a definition-matched peer or historical range, and do outcomes support concern?
Is the funding temporary, recurring, dedicated, debt-financed, or paired with a durable offset?

funding_types.use: Continuing legal obligation or durable service whose need persists across cycles.
funding_types.review: annual performance review plus multiyear structural review

funding_types.use: Acute backlog, shock, repair, transition, capacity, or geographically concentrated harm.
Known cyclical or contingent risks such as disasters or downturns.

current_evaluation.reason: Each lane has a source-custodied anchor and partial outcome-floor work, but complete common-year outcomes, policy-specific marginal effects, cross-lane normalization, delivery capacity, and cost-shift evidence are not yet available.

required_inputs: profile changes stated on the same year and general-government perimeter
one COFOG owner and amount for every savings and reinvestment item
updated common denominator after each profile
separate temporary and structural funding treatment
same_perimeter_peer_bridge.interpretation: Health and defense changes point toward the displayed peer ranges; social-protection and economic-affairs allocations may do so when current pain supports them. Education is already at the top of the displayed range and receives no automatic increase.

decision_rules: No peer gap by itself creates a cut or an appropriation.
No high program total by itself proves overfunding.
No poor outcome by itself proves that more money is the best remedy.
A lane may receive zero reserve dollars in a cycle, including education.
Temporary funding sunsets unless renewed on refreshed evidence.
Savings enter the rate model only after owner attribution, overlap removal, transition costs, floor passage, and whole-system reconciliation.
